issue.title: Batch save() silently deletes many-to-many junction rows of entities saved without their relation loaded (v1.0 regression)
sqljs measures query execution time before the statement runs
issue.body:
### Issue description

On the sqljs driver, query execution time is measured before the statement runs, so `maxQueryExecutionTime` never fires and the `afterQuery` event carries a wrong `executionTime`.

### Expected Behavior

`executionTime` covers the time the query actually took, and a query slower than `maxQueryExecutionTime` reaches `logQuerySlow`.

Every other query runner takes `queryEndTime` after the execution call has returned. Postgres measures after `await databaseConnection.query(...)`, better-sqlite3 after `stmt.all()` / `stmt.run()`, expo after `await statement.executeAsync()`, react-native and nativescript inside the completion callback, spanner after `await executor.run(...)`.

### Actual Behavior

`SqljsQueryRunner.query()` takes `queryEndTime` right after `prepare()` and `bind()`. In sql.js the statement runs while `step()` is iterated, and that loop sits below the measurement, so only the preparation is timed.

```ts
const queryStartTime = Date.now()
    statement = databaseConnection.prepare(query)
    statement.bind(parameters)
const queryEndTime = Date.now()          // measurement ends here
    if (slow) logQuerySlow(...)          // and the check runs here
    while (statement.step()) { ... }     // the query actually runs here
    broadcastAfterQueryEvent(..., queryExecutionTime, ...)
```

A query that takes 393 ms of wall clock reports 3 ms, and never reaches `logQuerySlow`:

```
sqljs
  afterQuery executionTime   3
  actual elapsed           393
  logQuerySlow             not called

better-sqlite3 (same query, same options)
  logQuerySlow             150
  afterQuery executionTime 150
  actual elapsed           150
```

### Steps to reproduce

```js
const { DataSource } = require('typeorm')

// all of the work happens inside step(), so preparation and execution are separable
const slow = `WITH RECURSIVE counter(x) AS (
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x + 1 FROM counter WHERE x < 2000000
) SELECT count(*) AS total FROM counter`

class Recorder {
    logQuery() {}
    logQueryError() {}
    logSchemaBuild() {}
    logMigration() {}
    log() {}
    logQuerySlow(time) {
        console.log('  logQuerySlow', time)
    }
}

class Sub {
    afterQuery(event) {
        console.log('  afterQuery executionTime', event.executionTime)
    }
}

async function run(type, extra) {
    const dataSource = new DataSource({
        type,
        maxQueryExecutionTime: 50,
        logger: new Recorder(),
        entities: [],
        ...extra,
    })
    await dataSource.initialize()
    dataSource.subscribers.push(new Sub())

    console.log(type)
    const started = Date.now()
    await dataSource.query(slow)
    console.log('  actual elapsed', Date.now() - started)

    await dataSource.destroy()
}

run('sqljs').then(() => run('better-sqlite3', { database: ':memory:' }))
```

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    | macOS 15.7.7 |
| Node.js version     | 22.16.0  |
| Typescript version  | 5.9.3    |
| TypeORM version     | master (04ff4dae) |
| sql.js version      | 1.14.1   |

### Additional Context

Two things break because of this.

1. `maxQueryExecutionTime` is effectively inert on sqljs. Preparation is sub-millisecond, so the threshold is never crossed no matter how slow the query is.
2. Anything consuming `AfterQueryEvent.executionTime` for instrumentation gets a value that has nothing to do with the query.

Issue #10180 covered a different case, mysql2 queueing the query after `queryStartTime` was taken, and was closed by the stale bot rather than resolved. This one is the opposite end of the same measurement, and is specific to sqljs.

PR #12750 changes the clock source on these two lines from `Date.now()` to `PlatformTools.performanceNow()`. It leaves the measurement point where it is, so it does not affect this.

issue.title: better-sqlite3 does not await query event subscribers and never reports failed queries
issue.body:
### Issue description

The better-sqlite3 query runner broadcasts the query events but never waits for the subscribers, and it never reports failed queries to them.

### Expected Behavior

`beforeQuery` subscribers settle before the query runs, `afterQuery` subscribers settle before `query()` resolves or rejects, and a failed query broadcasts `afterQuery` with `success` set to false. This is what every other runner that implements these events does, and it is the contract #11085 established.

### Actual Behavior

`BetterSqlite3QueryRunner.query()` calls `broadcastBeforeQueryEvent()` directly instead of awaiting the `BeforeQuery` broadcast, and `broadcasterResult.wait()` does not appear anywhere in the file. Running the driver against a stub connection with an async subscriber shows the ordering, with sqljs alongside for comparison:

```
better-sqlite3                sqljs
1. QUERY EXECUTED             1. beforeQuery settled
2. query() resolved           2. QUERY EXECUTED
3. beforeQuery settled        3. afterQuery settled
4. afterQuery settled         4. query() resolved
```

So an async `beforeQuery` hook runs after the query it is meant to precede, and `query()` resolves while `afterQuery` is still running. Since nothing awaits the returned promise, a subscriber that rejects becomes an unhandled rejection, which ends the process under Node's default behaviour.

Two related problems in the same method:

1. The `catch` block never broadcasts `afterQuery` with `success` set to false. Among the runners that broadcast these events, better-sqlite3 is the only one missing that call, so subscribers are told nothing when a query fails.
2. `getStmt()` sits outside the `try`, so a statement that fails to prepare throws the raw driver error instead of `QueryFailedError`:

```
                better-sqlite3        sqljs
error type      SqliteError           QueryFailedError
afterQuery      not broadcast         success: false
```

This looks like an oversight rather than an intentional difference. #11086 fixed the awaiting problem across 13 runners, including the old `sqlite` one, but better-sqlite3 is not in that PR's file list. #11836 later dropped `sqlite3` and made better-sqlite3 the default SQLite driver, so the runner that missed the fix became the one most people use.

The regression test added by #11086 uses `enabledDrivers: ["postgres"]`, which is why this went unnoticed.

### Steps to reproduce

Add better-sqlite3 to the existing regression test for #11085:

```ts
// test/github-issues/11085/issue-11085.test.ts
dataSources = await createTestingConnections({
    enabledDrivers: ["postgres", "better-sqlite3"],
    entities: [__dirname + "/entity/*{.js,.ts}"],
    subscribers: [__dirname + "/subscriber/*{.js,.ts}"],
})
```

It fails on master with `AssertionError: expected +0 to equal 1`, because the `beforeQuery` subscriber inserts the row after the select has already run.

### My Environment

| Dependency | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Operating System | macOS 15.7.7 |
| Node.js version | v22.16.0 |
| Typeorm | master (04ff4daed) and 1.1.0 |
| Database Driver & Version | better-sqlite3 12.11.1 |

### Additional Context

Reading `1.1.0` confirms the same state, so this is not limited to master.

Separately, if an `afterQuery` subscriber rejects, the `finally { await broadcasterResult.wait() }` used by the sibling runners lets that rejection replace the original `QueryFailedError`. That is a family wide behaviour rather than something specific to better-sqlite3, and #12724 already raises it, so I have kept it out of scope here.

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

- [x] better-sqlite3

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time and I know how to start.

issue.title: DataSource.initialize() leaks connections on concurrent calls and on cache connection failure
issue.body:
### Issue description

`DataSource.initialize()` leaks database connections when called concurrently, and when the query result cache fails to connect

### Expected Behavior

1. Calling `initialize()` while a previous `initialize()` call is still in flight should not open a second driver connection/pool. It should either reject (like calling `initialize()` on an already-initialized DataSource does) or coalesce with the in-flight attempt.
2. If `queryResultCache.connect()` fails during `initialize()`, the driver connection that was opened just before it should be closed before the error propagates, leaving the DataSource fully un-initialized.

### Actual Behavior

1. **Concurrent `initialize()` calls both connect the driver.** The `isInitialized` guard is only assigned *after* `driver.connect()` resolves, so two overlapping calls both pass the check and each open a driver connection/pool. Both calls resolve successfully, `destroy()` only closes the pool the driver currently references, and the other pool leaks.

2. **A cache connection failure leaks the driver connection.** In `initialize()`, `queryResultCache.connect()` runs after `driver.connect()` but *before* the cleanup `try/catch` begins. If the cache fails to connect (e.g. Redis is unreachable), `initialize()` rejects with the driver still connected — and it cannot be released afterwards, because `destroy()` throws `CannotExecuteNotConnectedError` while `isInitialized` is still `false`.

### Steps to reproduce

Both leaks reproduce with plain TypeORM and any driver; `better-sqlite3` shown for a dependency-free example, but the same happens with pooled drivers like `postgres` (where the leak means orphaned server connections).

**1. Concurrent initialization:**

```ts
import { DataSource } from "typeorm"

const dataSource = new DataSource({
    type: "better-sqlite3",
    database: ":memory:",
})

// e.g. two request handlers racing to lazily initialize the same DataSource
await Promise.all([dataSource.initialize(), dataSource.initialize()])
// driver.connect() has now run twice; both calls resolved successfully.
// With a pooled driver (postgres/mysql), one pool is orphaned and its
// connections are never released by destroy().
```

**2. Cache connection failure:**

```ts
import { DataSource } from "typeorm"

const dataSource = new DataSource({
    type: "postgres",
    host: "localhost",
    username: "test",
    password: "test",
    database: "test",
    cache: {
        type: "redis",
        options: { socket: { host: "unreachable-host", connectTimeout: 1000 } },
    },
})

try {
    await dataSource.initialize() // rejects: Redis is unreachable
} catch (error) {
    // the postgres pool opened by driver.connect() is still open here
    await dataSource.destroy() // throws CannotExecuteNotConnectedError
}
// no way to release the leaked pool; the process keeps the sockets open
```

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version    |
| ---                 | ---        |
| Operating System    | Windows 11 |
| Node.js version     | 22.17.1    |
| Typescript version  | 5.9.3      |
| TypeORM version     | 1.1.0 (reproduced on current `master`) |

### Additional Context

The root cause is the ordering inside `DataSource.initialize()` (`src/data-source/DataSource.ts`): the `isInitialized` flag is only set after `driver.connect()` and `queryResultCache.connect()` have both succeeded, and the cleanup `try/catch` only covers the steps *after* the flag assignment. Everything between the initial guard and that point is unprotected against both re-entry and failure.

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

All drivers — the bug is in driver-agnostic `DataSource` code (reproduced with `better-sqlite3` and `postgres`).

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start — PR incoming.

issue.title: CockroachDB: DataSource.destroy() hangs with multiple connected query runners
issue.body:
### Issue description

With the CockroachDB driver, `DataSource.destroy()` never resolves when two connected query runners are still held, even after both queries have completed. The shutdown loop releases the first runner but skips the second, leaving `pg-pool.end()` waiting for a checked-out connection.

Reproduced against current `master` (`b1eafc23d8d695a2e2f4ebe9063d9a0c92415d1d`) with a real CockroachDB server, not mocked connections.

### Expected behavior

`destroy()` releases all tracked query runners, closes the pool, and resolves. This matches the existing shutdown implementation and regression test for PostgreSQL, fixed in #7596 for #6958.

### Actual behavior

`destroy()` remains pending. With two connected query runners, the first has `isReleased === true`, while the second remains checked out. Applications awaiting database shutdown can consequently hang.

### Reproduction

Start a local server:

```sh
docker run --rm --name typeorm-cockroach-repro -p 127.0.0.1:26257:26257 cockroachdb/cockroach:v25.2.23 start-single-node --insecure
```

Run this against TypeORM built from the commit above:

```ts
import { DataSource } from "typeorm"

async function reproduce() {
    const dataSource = new DataSource({
        type: "cockroachdb",
        host: "127.0.0.1",
        port: 26257,
        username: "root",
        database: "defaultdb",
    })
    await dataSource.initialize()

    const firstRunner = dataSource.createQueryRunner()
    const secondRunner = dataSource.createQueryRunner()
    await firstRunner.query("SELECT 1")
    await secondRunner.query("SELECT 2")

    // Both queries have finished; no transaction or query is running.
    await dataSource.destroy()
    console.log("Destroyed") // Never reached on current master.
}

reproduce().catch(console.error)
```

### Cause and proposed fix

`CockroachDriver.closePool()` calls `connectedQueryRunners.map(runner => runner.release())`. Releasing a runner synchronously splices it out of that same array. Starting with `[first, second]`, releasing `first` moves `second` to index 0, so `map()` skips it when advancing to index 1. `Promise.all()` cannot wait for a release that was never invoked.

Use the same loop already present in `PostgresDriver.closePool()`:

```ts
while (this.connectedQueryRunners.length) {
    await this.connectedQueryRunners[0].release()
}
```

This preserves the existing intent to release all tracked runners before ending the pool; it does not introduce a new graceful-shutdown policy or wait for active application work.

### Verification and related work

- Enabled the existing `test/github-issues/6958/issue-6958.test.ts` regression for `cockroachdb` as well as `postgres`.
- Before the driver change: the test times out after 5 seconds in `destroy()`; subsequent teardown reports `Called end on pool more than once`.
- After the loop change: the same test passes against live CockroachDB.
- #7596 fixes the PostgreSQL implementation; CockroachDB still has the old loop. #7823 is another historical PostgreSQL report. Merged #11523 changes disconnect error handling but leaves this loop unchanged. I found no matching CockroachDB fix in the public issue/PR searches.

### Environment

- TypeORM: source build of master `b1eafc23d8d695a2e2f4ebe9063d9a0c92415d1d`
- CockroachDB: v25.2.23, Linux container, single node
- Node.js: v22.17.1 on Windows
- pg: 8.23.0; pg-pool: 3.14.0
- Driver: `cockroachdb`

I can submit the minimal fix and extend the existing regression test.

issue.title: Composite string primary keys containing underscores collapse distinct entities during hydration
Inconsistent default relation options with `@ManyToMany` relations
Database cache remove() leaks its query runner after a deletion fails
issue.body:
### Issue description

`DbQueryResultCache.remove()` releases its internally created query runner only when every deletion succeeds. A rejected `DELETE` bypasses release and can exhaust the connection pool. This is a remaining failure-path gap after earlier cache cleanup fixes.

### Expected Behavior

Return an owned connection after removal fails, preserve the deletion error, and keep caller-supplied runners under caller ownership. Any other deletions already started on the runner must settle before the connection is returned to the pool.

### Actual Behavior

`await Promise.all(...)` rejects before the release statement. A straightforward `finally` alone also needs care: `Promise.all()` rejects as soon as one operation fails, while other operations can still be using that runner.

### Steps to reproduce

Use a disposable PostgreSQL database: this script deliberately removes its test cache table to make the deletion fail.

```ts
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm'

const source = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres', url: process.env.POSTGRES_URL,
  cache: true, synchronize: true,
  extra: { max: 1, connectionTimeoutMillis: 1000 },
})
await source.initialize()
try {
  await source.query('DROP TABLE "query-result-cache"')
  await source.queryResultCache!.remove(['first', 'second'])
    .catch(error => console.log(error.message)) // Missing-table error.
  await source.query('SELECT 1') // Currently times out acquiring a connection.
} finally {
  await source.destroy()
}
```

This is not limited to a missing table: a separate reproduction holds a conflicting table lock and causes a statement timeout. After releasing that lock, PostgreSQL is healthy but the cache removal connection remains checked out.

### My Environment

Current master `c64a1f052fc39f6688b6b73b83d065d7147ba8bb`; Node.js 22.17.1; PostgreSQL 15.6. The affected cache implementation is shared across relational drivers.

### Additional Context / proposed fix

Protect construction/execution of the deletion operations with cleanup. On rejection, settle the already-started operations, attempt release of an internally created runner, and rethrow the original deletion error even if cleanup also fails. After successful deletion, release an internally created runner normally and surface any cleanup error. Caller-supplied runners remain caller-owned. Keep the existing per-identifier SQL and parallel scheduling on success. This adds no queries, parameter-limit changes, or new dependencies; the extra settlement pass is restricted to failures.

Related history: #3370/#4866 reported earlier cache connection problems; merged #8969 added release on successful removal. Merged #12797 protects `clear()`/`getFromCache()`, and #12545 protects `storeInCache()`. None covers this remaining `remove()` error path.

Regression tests cover empty/single/multiple identifiers, successful and rejected operations, supplied-runner ownership, a deferred second deletion after the first fails, cleanup errors, and real PostgreSQL failure followed by a successful query. The owned-error and pending-deletion assertions fail on unchanged master. With the fix, all 19 focused cache tests pass, including the existing query-builder cache suite. The broader unit and functional-cache run has 164 passing and 4 pending tests.

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes.

issue.title: Postgres: unconditional nested join parentheses in 1.1.0 constrain the planner and regress query plans
`deepValue()` throws when find options omit an embedded that holds an eager relation
SQL Server query subscriber failures retain the query-runner lock
issue.body:
### Issue description

SQL Server's query runner can retain its FIFO query lock when a query subscriber fails. Every later query on that runner then waits indefinitely, even after removing the failing subscriber.

### Expected Behavior

Continue awaiting subscribers, propagate their error, and release the acquired query lock on every failure path. A failing `beforeQuery` must still prevent the database request from executing.

### Actual Behavior

- `beforeQuery` is awaited after acquiring the lock but outside the protected `try` block. A thrown or rejected hook skips release.
- `afterQuery` promises are awaited in `finally`, before `release()`. A rejected hook skips the release statement.

### Steps to reproduce

For a SQL Server data source, run this after initialization. Repeat with `afterQuery` instead of `beforeQuery` to exercise the second path:

```ts
const queryRunner = source.createQueryRunner()
source.subscribers.push({
  async beforeQuery() { throw new Error('subscriber failed') },
})
await queryRunner.query('SELECT 1 AS value').catch(error => console.log(error.message))
source.subscribers.length = 0

console.log(await Promise.race([
  queryRunner.query('SELECT 1 AS value'),
  new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve('still waiting for lock'), 1000)),
]))
// Actual: "still waiting for lock". Expected: [{ value: 1 }].
```

### My Environment

Current master `c64a1f052fc39f6688b6b73b83d065d7147ba8bb`, Node.js 22.17.1. Driver: SQL Server.

The regression tests execute the real `SqlServerQueryRunner`, `Broadcaster`, and `QueryLock`, with only the mssql connection/request transport stubbed. The before-hook failure occurs before any driver request. I have not run these cases against a live SQL Server instance.

### Additional Context / proposed fix

Release and rethrow if logging/pre-query broadcasting fails. Put the post-query subscriber wait inside `try/finally` so it always releases the lock. Preserve the existing subscriber order, error propagation, and database error handling. This adds no queries, timers, lock acquisitions, or async boundaries on the successful path.

The tests cover synchronous and asynchronous failures for both events, a subsequent successful query on the same runner, holding the lock while successful hooks are pending, and database-request errors. Three cases fail on unchanged master; all seven pass with the fix.

Merged #11086 intentionally waits for asynchronous `beforeQuery` hooks; this fix preserves that behavior. #11540 is also merged but does not protect these two lock-release paths. Searches did not locate an existing report/fix or a maintainer deferral for this exact failure.

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes.

issue.title: PostgreSQL driver doesnt read Z and M Geometry suffixes from coord_dimension
issue.body:
### Issue description

When loading tables form DB and using PostGIS, PostgreSQL driver doesnt take into account coord_dimension column of geometry_columns table. Therefore when using specific geometry spatialFeatureType like `GeometryZ` TypeORM generates migration to this type over and over again.

### Expected Behavior

Translate coord_dimension and type columns of geometry columns table into correct `spatialFeatureType`
ie
|coord_dimension|type|spatialFeatureType|
|---|---|---|
|2|GEOMETRY|Geometry|
|3|GEOMETRY|GeometryZ|
|3|GEOMETRYM|GeometryM|
|4|GEOMETRY|GeometryZM|


### Actual Behavior

Only type field is taken into account, so if I create a table with `GeometryZ` column, generate migration and apply it, all following generated migrations will still have this change included, despite columns being already GeometryZ:
```ts
public async up(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    await queryRunner.query(`ALTER TABLE "test" ALTER COLUMN "geometry" TYPE geometry(geometryz,5514)`);
}

public async down(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    await queryRunner.query(`ALTER TABLE "test" ALTER COLUMN "geometry" TYPE geometry(GEOMETRY,5514)`);
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

* create entity with GeometryZ column
  `@Column({ type: "geometry", spatialFeatureType: "geometryz", srid: 5514 })`
* generate migration
* run migrations
* generate migration again
* see typeorm trying to ALTER COLUMN geometry again to GeometryZ, despite it being already GeometryZ

issue.title: MSSQL: lock table hint emitted outside nested join parentheses, producing invalid SQL (1.1.0 regression)
issue.body:
### Issue description

mssql + TypeORM 1.1.0: a lock combined with a two-level relation join emits WITH (NOLOCK) outside the nested join's parentheses, so the query fails with Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'with'. 1.1.0 regression.

### Expected Behavior

A query with a relation chain of depth >= 2 and `setLock()` should produce valid T-SQL,
with the table hint attached to each table reference.

### Actual Behavior

The hint is appended after the closing `)` of the nested join, where a table hint is not
allowed, and the inner table loses its hint entirely. SQL Server fails with:

```
QueryFailedError: Error: Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'with'. If this statement is a
common table expression, an xmlnamespaces clause or a change tracking context clause, the
previous statement must be terminated with a semicolon.
```

### Steps to reproduce

Entities (three distinct entities, plain many-to-one — nothing special about them):

```ts
@Entity() class Country { @PrimaryColumn() id: number }

@Entity() class Profile {
  @PrimaryColumn() id: number
  @Column() countryId: number
  @ManyToOne(() => Country) @JoinColumn({ name: 'countryId' }) country: Country
}

@Entity() class User {
  @PrimaryColumn() id: number
  @Column() profileId: number
  @ManyToOne(() => Profile) @JoinColumn({ name: 'profileId' }) profile: Profile
}
```

Depth 1 — **valid**:

```ts
repo.createQueryBuilder('u').leftJoinAndSelect('u.profile', 'p').setLock('dirty_read')
```
```sql
FROM "user" "u" WITH (NOLOCK) LEFT JOIN "profile" "p" WITH (NOLOCK) ON "p"."id"="u"."profileId"
```

Depth 2 — **invalid**:

```ts
repo.createQueryBuilder('u')
  .leftJoinAndSelect('u.profile', 'p')
  .leftJoinAndSelect('p.country', 'c')
  .setLock('dirty_read')
```
```sql
FROM "user" "u" WITH (NOLOCK) LEFT JOIN ("profile" "p" LEFT JOIN "country" "c" WITH (NOLOCK) ON "c"."id"="p"."countryId") WITH (NOLOCK) ON "p"."id"="u"."profileId"
--                            ^ hint missing on "p"                                                                    ^ hint illegal here
```

Also reproduces through find options, so it is not query-builder specific:

```ts
repo.find({ relations: { profile: { country: true } }, lock: { mode: 'dirty_read' } })
```

And with the other two lock modes — `pessimistic_read` → `WITH (HOLDLOCK, ROWLOCK)`,
`pessimistic_write` → `WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK)` — in the same wrong position.

Depth 2 *without* a lock is valid, so the parenthesised nesting itself is fine; only the
hint placement is wrong.


### My Environment

| Dependency | Version |
| --- | --- |
| operating system | Linux |
| typeorm | 1.1.0 (works on 1.0.0 and 0.3.29) |
| driver | mssql |


### Additional Context

Regression appeared between 1.0.0 and 1.1.0: on 1.0.0 and 0.3.29 the same code emits every
join flat, with no parentheses, so the hint is always attached to a table reference.

issue.title: save() does not update a utc: true date column when the process runs west of UTC
issue.body:
### Issue description

`save()` does not write a changed `{ type: "date", utc: true }` column when the process runs west of UTC

### Expected Behavior

Loading an entity, setting its `utc: true` date column to `new Date(Date.UTC(2025, 5, 1))` and calling `save()` stores `2025-06-01`, the same as `update()` does with that value.

### Actual Behavior

With `TZ=America/New_York`, `save()` sends no UPDATE and the column keeps `2025-05-31`. `update()` with the same Date writes `2025-06-01`. With `TZ=UTC` or `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`, `save()` sends the UPDATE.

Output of the script below, the same on better-sqlite3 and postgres:

```
TZ=America/New_York stored 2025-05-31; save(utcDate = 2025-06-01T00:00Z) sent 0 UPDATE -> db 2025-05-31; control update() -> db 2025-06-01
TZ=UTC              stored 2025-05-31; save(utcDate = 2025-06-01T00:00Z) sent 1 UPDATE -> db 2025-06-01; control update() -> db 2025-06-01
TZ=Asia/Tokyo       stored 2025-05-31; save(utcDate = 2025-06-01T00:00Z) sent 1 UPDATE -> db 2025-06-01; control update() -> db 2025-06-01
```

### Steps to reproduce

```ts
@Entity()
class Event {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id: number

    @Column({ type: "date", utc: true })
    utcDate: Date | string
}

// run with TZ=America/New_York
const repo = dataSource.getRepository(Event)
const { id } = await repo.save({ utcDate: "2025-05-31" })

const event = await repo.findOneByOrFail({ id })
event.utcDate = new Date(Date.UTC(2025, 5, 1))
await repo.save(event) // no UPDATE is sent

const row = await repo.findOneByOrFail({ id })
console.log(row.utcDate) // "2025-05-31", expected "2025-06-01"
```

The change detector formats the new value without the column's `utc` option:

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/5d5fc38f70903f7933779d194bc2dd1e15d83e7a/packages/typeorm/src/persistence/SubjectChangedColumnsComputer.ts#L110-L122

In New York, `2025-06-01T00:00Z` is still May 31 local time, so it formats as `2025-05-31`, equal to the stored value, and the column is marked unchanged. The write path formats with `{ utc: columnMetadata.utc }` (for example `PostgresDriver.preparePersistentValue`), so `update()` stores `2025-06-01`.

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    | Ubuntu Linux |
| Node.js version     | 22.23.3  |
| Typescript version  | 5.9.3    |
| TypeORM version     | 1.1.1 (master 5d5fc38f7) |
| better-sqlite3      | 12.11.1  |
| pg                  | 8.23.0 (PostgreSQL 17.11) |

### Additional Context

The `utc` option came in #11740, which passes it to `DateUtils.mixedDateToDateString` on every driver's write path. The change detector is the one call that does not. The fix is to pass `{ utc: column.utc }` to the scalar `mixedDateToDateString` call in `SubjectChangedColumnsComputer`. `date[]` columns stay as they are, because their write path does not apply `utc` either. I can open a PR with a failing test in `test/functional/columns/date-utc/`.

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

- [x] better-sqlite3
- [x] postgres

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start.

issue.title: OrmUtils.normalizeWhereCriteria() does not implement described default behaviour for invalidWhereValuesBehavior
issue.body: ### Issue description If the DataSource is not configured with invalidWhereValuesBehavior, OrmUtils.normalizeWhereCriteria() does not throw by default. ### Expected Behavior If invalidWhereValuesBehavior is not set, OrmUtils.normalizeWhereCriteria() should implement the default behaviour described in the docs, i.e. it should throw an error. https://typeorm.io/docs/data-source/null-and-undefined-handling#throw-default-1 > 'throw' (default) > JavaScript undefined values cause a TypeORMError to be thrown: ### Actual Behavior Currently, if no options are set in the DataSource then the criteria is returned immediately. ``` static normalizeWhereCriteria( criteria: ObjectLiteral, options?: { null?: "ignore" | "sql-null" | "throw" undefined?: "ignore" | "throw" }, path?: string, ): ObjectLiteral { if (!options) return criteria ``` https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/1.0.0/src/util/OrmUtils.ts#L670 So, UPDATE queries are still executed with buggy filters, e.g. `UPDATE "schema_x"."table_y" SET "col1" = $1 WHERE "col2" = null` with no warning/error for the dev to detect this easily. ### Steps to reproduce https://github.com/samkessaram/typeorm-undefined-where-bug ```bash git clone https://github.com/samkessaram/typeorm-undefined-where-bug.git cd typeorm-undefined-where-bug npm install npm start ``` ### My Environment | Dependency | Version | | --- | --- | | Operating System | MacOS | | Node.js version | 24.16.0 | | Typescript version | 5.9.3 | | TypeORM version | 1.0.0 | | @nestjs/typeorm | 11.0.1 | ### Additional Context **_Risk_**: If invalidWhereValuesBehavior: { undefined: "ignore" } is later added (e.g. during a version upgrade), the update() path changes from "silent no-op" to "unscoped UPDATE affecting ALL rows" — with no intermediate error state to catch it. ### Relevant Database Driver(s) - issue.title: insert() / save() start an unawaited lazy-relation query when a join column is also a primary column
Replace Date.now() with performance.now() in query() method
issue.body: Replace `Date.now()` with `performance.now()` when measuring query execution time in `QueryRunner.query()`. `performance.now()` provides a monotonic, higher-resolution timer that's better suited for measuring elapsed durations.

issue.title: Closure-table reparenting leaves stale ancestors when a primary column is renamed
Auto-created STI discriminator index is silently dropped when the entity has an embedded column
issue.body:
### Issue description

The index TypeORM auto-creates on a single-table-inheritance discriminator column is silently dropped when the STI base entity has at least one embedded column and at least one generated column.

### Expected Behavior

An STI base entity declared with `@TableInheritance()` gets an index on its discriminator column, as `EntityMetadataBuilder.createKeysForTableInheritance()` intends, regardless of whether the entity also has embedded columns.

### Actual Behavior

With an embedded column (`@Column(() => Something)`) present alongside a generated column (e.g. `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn()`), the discriminator index is missing from `EntityMetadata.indices` and is therefore never created in the schema. No error and no warning is emitted — `synchronize`/migration generation simply produces a table without that index.

Root cause is an array-identity subtlety in `src/metadata-builder/EntityMetadataBuilder.ts`.

`computeEntityMetadataStep2()` derives `indices` from `ownIndices`:

```ts
entityMetadata.indices = entityMetadata.embeddeds.reduce(
    (indices, embedded) => indices.concat(embedded.indicesFromTree),
    entityMetadata.ownIndices,
)
```

- With **zero** embeddeds, `Array.prototype.reduce` with an initial value and an empty array returns the initial value **by reference**, so `indices` *is* `ownIndices`.
- With **one or more** embeddeds, `concat` produces a **new** array, so `indices` is a copy that is no longer connected to `ownIndices`.

Later in `build()`, `createKeysForTableInheritance()` pushes the auto index onto `entityMetadata.indices`:

```ts
entityMetadata.indices.push(
    new IndexMetadata({ entityMetadata, columns: [entityMetadata.discriminatorColumn!], ... }),
)
```

In the zero-embedded case that push also lands in `ownIndices` (same array), so it survives. In the embedded case it lands only on the detached copy.

`build()` then re-runs `computeEntityMetadataStep2()` for every entity that has a generated column:

```ts
if (generated) {
    ...
    column.build(this.dataSource)
    this.computeEntityMetadataStep2(entityMetadata)
}
```

That re-run reassigns `indices` from `ownIndices` + embedded indices, and the auto-created discriminator index is discarded.

So the bug needs all three of: STI base, ≥1 embedded column, ≥1 generated column. A `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn()` id — which nearly every entity has — supplies the third.

An explicit `@Index()` on the discriminator column is unaffected: it comes from metadata args into `ownIndices`, so it is recreated by every step-2 run. That is also why the existing dedup guard in `createKeysForTableInheritance()` (`isDiscriminatorColumnAlreadyIndexed`) still behaves correctly once the underlying bug is fixed — no double index for users who already added the decorator by hand.

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal reproduction (`better-sqlite3`, in-memory — the outcome is decided at the metadata layer, so every driver is affected):

```ts
import "reflect-metadata"
import {
    ChildEntity, Column, DataSource, Entity,
    PrimaryGeneratedColumn, TableInheritance,
} from "typeorm"

class Meta {
    @Column({ type: String, nullable: true })
    note?: string
}

@Entity({ name: "with_embedded" })
@TableInheritance({ column: { type: String, name: "discriminator" } })
class WithEmbedded {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id!: number

    @Column(() => Meta)
    meta!: Meta
}

@ChildEntity()
class WithEmbeddedChild extends WithEmbedded {}

@Entity({ name: "without_embedded" })
@TableInheritance({ column: { type: String, name: "discriminator" } })
class WithoutEmbedded {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id!: number
}

@ChildEntity()
class WithoutEmbeddedChild extends WithoutEmbedded {}

const ds = new DataSource({
    type: "better-sqlite3",
    database: ":memory:",
    entities: [WithEmbedded, WithEmbeddedChild, WithoutEmbedded, WithoutEmbeddedChild],
    synchronize: true,
})

await ds.initialize()

for (const target of [WithEmbedded, WithoutEmbedded]) {
    const metadata = ds.getMetadata(target)
    const indices = metadata.indices.filter(
        (index) =>
            index.columns.length === 1 &&
            index.columns[0].databaseName === "discriminator",
    )
    console.log(metadata.tableName, "discriminator indices:", indices.length)
}
```

Output on `master` (`ac41823b9`, 1.1.1):

```
with_embedded discriminator indices: 0
without_embedded discriminator indices: 1
```

Inspecting the created tables through a query runner gives the same result: the `with_embedded` table has no index on `discriminator`.

Removing the `@Column(() => Meta)` line makes the index appear. Removing `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn()` (using a plain primary column instead) also makes it appear, because nothing then triggers the second `computeEntityMetadataStep2()` run.

### My Environment

| Dependency         | Version                        |
| ---                | ---                            |
| Operating System   | macOS 15 (also Linux CI)       |
| Node.js version    | 24.14.1                        |
| Typescript version | 5.9.3                          |
| TypeORM version    | master `ac41823b9` (1.1.1), also 1.0.x and 0.3.x |

Affected on both active branches: the code shape is identical on `master` and on `v0` (`entityMetadata.indices = entityMetadata.embeddeds.reduce(...)` plus the post-hoc push in `createKeysForTableInheritance`). Verified reproducing on 0.3.28 and on 1.1.0 as well as current `master`.

### Additional Context

This is not a theoretical edge case. Any framework that adds an embedded column to a base entity hits it for every STI hierarchy it defines.

Vendure is the clearest example: every Vendure entity carries an embedded `customFields` column and a generated id, so **all** of its STI discriminator indexes are missing in every Vendure installation — `history_entry.discriminator`, `session.type`, `region.discriminator`, `stock_movement.discriminator`.

The production consequence on our own installation: a `history_entry` table of roughly 2M rows, with admin `COUNT` queries filtered by `discriminator` sequentially scanning it under peak load. Reported downstream as vendurehq/vendure#5286, with a workaround (explicit `@Index()` decorators on those discriminator columns) proposed in vendurehq/vendure#5287 — but the missing index originates here, and affects any application with this entity shape.

The fix looks small: make the auto-created index land in `ownIndices` (which every `computeEntityMetadataStep2()` run preserves) instead of in the derived `indices` array. I have a patch and tests and will open a PR against `master`.

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

All drivers — the index is dropped at the metadata layer, before any driver is involved.

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start.

issue.title: Postgres/CockroachDB: spatial columns without spatialFeatureType or srid generate an endless no-op migration
issue.body:
### Issue description

A geometry or geography column declared without `spatialFeatureType` or `srid` produces the same `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` statement on every `migration:generate`, even though nothing changed and running the generated migration is a no-op.

### Expected Behavior

Once the schema is in sync, `migration:generate` reports "No changes in database schema were found."

### Actual Behavior

Every run emits, for each such column:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "post" ALTER COLUMN "geom" TYPE geometry
ALTER TABLE "post" ALTER COLUMN "pointWithoutSRID" TYPE geometry(Point)
ALTER TABLE "post" ALTER COLUMN "geog" TYPE geography
```

This reproduces with the repository's own spatial test entity (`test/functional/spatial/postgres/entity/Post.ts`): logging the schema builder against it returns those three queries on PostGIS 3.6 and on CockroachDB v24.3.8 alike.

Cause: the column is created as plain `geometry`, which `geometry_columns` reports back as feature type `GEOMETRY` with SRID `0`, while the entity metadata keeps both undefined. `findChangedColumns` compares the raw values, so the column always looks changed. The decorator reference already documents those defaults ("If not specified, it will behave as though `Geometry` was provided" and "If not specified, it will default to `0`"); they are simply not applied in the comparison.

This is distinct from #12800, which is about `precision` on spatial columns.

### Steps to reproduce

```ts
@Entity()
export class Post {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id: number

    @Column("geometry", { nullable: true })
    geom: Geometry

    @Column("geometry", { nullable: true, spatialFeatureType: "Point" })
    pointWithoutSRID: Point

    @Column("geography", { nullable: true })
    geog: Geography
}
```

1. Synchronize or create the schema.
2. Run `migration:generate` (or `createSchemaBuilder().log()`): three `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` statements.
3. Apply them and generate again: the same three statements.

### My Environment

| Dependency | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Operating System | Linux |
| Node.js version | 22 |
| Typescript version | 5.x |
| TypeORM version | master (b495ed44) |

PostgreSQL 14.22 with PostGIS 3.6.2 (the CI image) and CockroachDB v24.3.8.

issue.title: Relation object assigned inside an embedded entity is silently not persisted when the join column is shared with an explicit column
issue.body:
### Issue description

Assigning a relation object inside an embedded entity is silently not persisted when the join column is shared with an explicitly declared column (the "relation id column" pattern: `@Column() avatarId` alongside `@ManyToOne() avatar`). The identical pattern on a top-level (non-embedded) property works correctly.

### Expected Behavior

Given an embedded class with both a relation and its explicit id column:

```ts
export class Profile {
    @ManyToOne(() => Avatar)
    avatar: Avatar

    @Column({ type: "int", nullable: true })
    avatarId: number
}

@Entity()
export class User {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id: number

    @Column(() => Profile)
    profile: Profile
}
```

assigning the relation and saving:

```ts
user.profile.avatar = avatar
await dataSource.getRepository(User).save(user)
```

should persist the foreign key, so that a reload yields `loaded.profile.avatarId === avatar.id` — matching the behavior of the same pattern on a non-embedded property.

### Actual Behavior

The foreign key column is not written and remains `NULL`. No error is thrown and no SQL is generated for the column — the assignment is silently dropped, on both INSERT and UPDATE.

The cause is in `ColumnMetadata.getEntityValue()`. The embedded-column branch resolves the relation value like this:

```ts
const embeddedObject = extractEmbeddedColumnValue(propertyNames, entity)
if (embeddedObject) {
    if (this.relationMetadata && this.referencedColumn) {
        const relatedEntity =
            this.relationMetadata.getEntityValue(embeddedObject)
```

It passes the already-extracted `embeddedObject`. However, `RelationMetadata.getEntityValue()` expects the **full entity** — it performs the embedded-path traversal itself via `this.embeddedMetadata.parentPropertyNames`. The result is a double traversal (effectively `entity.profile.profile.avatar`), so `relatedEntity` always resolves to `undefined`, and the code falls back to `embeddedObject[this.propertyName]` (`avatarId`), which a relation-object assignment does not populate. The column value resolves to `undefined` and the persistence layer skips it.

The non-embedded branch of the same method correctly passes `entity`, which is why the top-level pattern works.

The same mismatch breaks the update path: `Subject.createValueSetAndPopChangeMap()` produces a value map keyed by the relation property (`{ profile: { avatar: { id: 1 } } }`), and the per-column value extraction via `getEntityValue()` fails to resolve it for the same reason.

Suggested fix — pass the full entity, since `RelationMetadata.getEntityValue()` handles the embedded traversal internally:

```ts
const relatedEntity = this.relationMetadata.getEntityValue(entity)
```

With this change, the reproduction below passes, and the full test suite (better-sqlite3) passes with no regressions. I will submit a PR with the fix and regression tests.

### Steps to reproduce

Reproduction in the repository's own test format (fails on current master):

```ts
it("persists a relation object assigned inside an embedded", async () => {
    const avatar = await dataSource.getRepository(Avatar).save(new Avatar())

    const user = new User()
    user.profile = new Profile()
    user.profile.avatar = avatar
    await dataSource.getRepository(User).save(user)

    const loaded = await dataSource
        .getRepository(User)
        .findOneByOrFail({ id: user.id })
    expect(loaded.profile.avatarId).to.equal(avatar.id)
    // AssertionError: expected null to equal 1
})
```

Control test with the same pattern on a top-level property of the entity passes. A sanity check confirms the explicit `avatarId` column is correctly merged with the relation's join column (a single `ColumnMetadata` with one database column), so the failure is purely in value resolution, not in schema building.

### My Environment

| Dependency | Version |
| ---------- | ------- |
| Operating System | macOS (darwin arm64) |
| Node.js version | 24.14.1 |
| Typescript version | as per repo |
| TypeORM version | current master (1.0.0-dev, cca26a919); also reproduced on 0.3.28 |

### Additional Context

Discovered while implementing relation id columns for embedded custom fields in Vendure (https://github.com/vendurehq/vendure/issues/2031). In that context the bug was also observed with the sqlite (sql.js), postgres and mariadb drivers — it is driver-independent, as the defect is in the metadata/persistence layer.

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

- better-sqlite3 (used in the reproduction; affects all drivers)

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start.

issue.title: Build fails on version 1 due to failed resolution of expo-sqlite
issue.body:
### Issue description

Build fails on version 1 due to failed resolution of expo-sqlite

### Expected Behavior

After updating to typeorm version 1, expect `npm run build` of my application to succeed.

### Actual Behavior

Build fails with this error, even though my app does not use expo. It uses capacitor.
```
error during build:
Build failed with 1 error:

Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "expo-sqlite" from "/Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/typeorm/browser/driver/expo/ExpoDriver.js".
This is most likely unintended because it can break your application at runtime.
If you do want to externalize this module explicitly add it to
`build.rolldownOptions.external`
    at viteLog (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33346:57)
    at onRollupLog (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33378:7)
    at onLog (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33146:4)
    at file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/rolldown-build-CrPk_lZe.mjs:50:26
    at logger (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/rolldown-build-CrPk_lZe.mjs:41:3)
    at aggregateBindingErrorsIntoJsError (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/error-BuvQYXuZ.mjs:48:18)
    at unwrapBindingResult (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/error-BuvQYXuZ.mjs:18:128)
    at #build (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/rolldown-build-CrPk_lZe.mjs:3246:34)
    at async buildEnvironment (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33253:64)
    at async Object.build (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33675:19)
    at async Object.buildApp (file:///Users/jacob/repositories/f-next/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33672:153)

  errors: [Getter/Setter]
```

I am able to work around and get build to work by adding to vite.config.ts:
```
rolldownOptions: {
   external: ['expo-sqlite']
}
```
But it doesn't seem that this should be necessary, given that my app doesn't use expo and no other drivers have this issue. It seems unintended.
